name: Secured Finance same-block order-book unit price valued as collateral
summary: Secured Finance valued lend positions used as collateral with LendingMarket.getMarketUnitPrice, which returns the current block's filled amount divided by filled future value once block volume passes a fixed threshold. Attackers matched orders between two of their own accounts inside one transaction to set that price, so a cheaply bought lend position counted as fully backed collateral, and withdrew other depositors' USDC, WBTC, WETH and JPYC from the TokenVault on Ethereum and Arbitrum.
notes: Ninth and last pre-exploit Upgraded event of the LendingMarket beacon read by the market proxy, selecting implementation 0xd06dd40ba7c2cff3a6aa2f59c55d249aca57e521 with newly linked OrderActionLogic 0x41eb72013fd9b65fb9b9bbfa36894ca3a630750b; beacon.implementation() still returns it at block 25914034.

Exact net TokenVault outflow across nine successful Ethereum drains by four actors (blocks 25914035-25914841) and three Arbitrum drains by the anchor attacker (blocks 502170775-502171688), all exploiting the same order-book price in the same compiled LendingMarket template. Attacker and helper deposits made inside each transaction are netted out. Stablecoins at par; WBTC, WETH and JPYC at DefiLlama prices contemporaneous with each asset's largest drain. The DeFiHackLabs headline (~$104K) omits part of this campaign; the measured total is higher.
